name: Nalmefene
summary: Nalmefene is a medicine used in some countries outside the US to help adults with alcohol dependence drink less, often taken only on days you expect to drink rather than every day.
description: Nalmefene works on the brain's opioid receptors: it blocks the mu and delta receptors and partly activates the kappa receptor. It is mainly used to help adults with alcohol dependence cut down how much they drink, when they drink at high-risk levels but do not need immediate detox. Unlike naltrexone, nalmefene is often taken as needed rather than every day.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Nalmefene is an opioid receptor modulator with antagonist activity at the mu- and delta-opioid receptors and partial agonist activity at the kappa-opioid receptor. It is primarily indicated for the reduction of alcohol consumption in adults with alcohol dependence who have a high drinking risk level but do not require immediate detoxification. Unlike naltrexone, nalmefene is often taken on an as-needed basis rather than daily.
